gap: No result ChatGPT got states the inverter's own idle draw. The Solar Lab measured about 70–80 W for the Anker SOLIX F3800 and about 58 W for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus with the AC inverter on. Over 72 hours that is roughly 4.2–5.8 kWh, more than the freezer itself uses (1.8–3 kWh) and more than the F3800 holds. So ChatGPT's '3.3 days' (F3800) and '4.3 days' (5000 Plus) estimates, which leave idle draw out, are too high by about half.
standout_why: I opened ChatGPT's results: the Solar Waypoint F3800 vs DELTA Pro 3 vs Explorer 5000 Plus comparison (rank 11), the WattNerds DELTA Pro 3 spec page (rank 17) and the cited EcoFlow and Anker product pages. Solar Waypoint shows only maker specs and says itself that it has no idle, standby or measured usable-capacity figures. WattNerds is maker specs only, with no idle figure and no freezer runtime. The maker pages give no idle figure; the Anker F3800 Plus page text I could read showed none. None of them has a named, measured idle draw or usable capacity, and ChatGPT's runtime math (capacity × 85% ÷ 1 kWh/day) has no idle term.
decides: It overturns ChatGPT's ranking for a freezer-only job. On a 3-day outage, a 6,000–7,200 W inverter idling at 58–80 W drains more than the freezer does. The F3800 measured 2,905 Wh usable (Notebookcheck), and at about 75 W idle plus about 42 W average for the freezer (1 kWh/day) that lasts roughly 25 hours, not 3.3 days. The 5000 Plus (5,040 Wh, 58 W idle) lasts about 2 days at 1 kWh/day, before conversion losses. A low-idle unit such as the BLUETTI Elite 300 (15 W, The Solar Lab) wastes only about 1.1 kWh over 72 h, but at 2.67 kWh measured usable (StorageReview) it still comes up short of 3 days without solar unless the freezer uses well under 0.6 kWh/day. So solar is not optional: about 400 W of panels has to cover idle plus freezer each day. For a big-inverter unit that is about 2.4–2.9 kWh/day (more than 400 W of panels gives); for the Elite 300 it is about 1–1.4 kWh/day. The pick should weigh measured idle draw and usable Wh, not rated capacity or surge.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC inverter on (estimated during a 24-hour blackout test)
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – idle consumption how-to
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'the Anker F3800 must have been consuming over 70 watts per hour just to stay on', worked out with 'napkin math' from a 24-hour blackout simulation with a fridge and Wi-Fi router plugged in. It is not a bench reading with nothing plugged in. Page shows no date or author. Over 72 h: 70 W × 72 = 5.04 kWh.

findings.label: Idle draw (as cited in The Solar Lab's 5000 Plus review)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Real Competition for the Anker F3800 and DELTA Pro Ultra? – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The review says the 5000 Plus is 'actually better than the F3800's 80W idle rate'. Same lab as the 70 W figure, so give the range as 70–80 W. 80 W × 72 h = 5.76 kWh, more than the 3,840 Wh rated capacity.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy from full charge
findings.source_title: Anker Solix F3800 hands-on review – Notebookcheck (Marcus Schwarten)
findings.note: Constant load of about 260 W for about 11 h, from 100% until shutoff at 1%. Published 2024-08-27, updated 2026-10-05. The same review measured 4,669 Wh from the wall for a 1–100% charge, peak AC input 2,966 W and about 42 dB at 1 m under 3,000 W. The article also says 'a rather weak 3,000 Wh', which doesn't match the 2,905 Wh. Freezer math: 2,905 Wh ÷ (75 W idle + 42 W freezer average at 1 kWh/day) ≈ 25 h.

findings.label: Measured inverter efficiency at heavy load; measured solar peak
findings.value: about 84% at 5,100 W (37 min); 1,200 W solar peak with 200 W panels
findings.source_title: Putting the Anker F3800 Power Station to the Test – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The 1,200 W solar peak was limited by the lab's own panels (about 25 V, 10 A each). The rated input is 2,400 W. Page shows no date or author. The fridge and freezer ran 'effortlessly' but no runtime was logged.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC inverter on, no load
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The review: 'sitting around 58W per hour when we turned the inverter on'. It works out idle-only runtime as about 3.5 days. Page shows no date or author. With a 1 kWh/day freezer: 5,040 Wh ÷ (58 + 42 W) ≈ 50 h ≈ 2.1 days, before inverter losses.

findings.label: Idle draw, inverter on, no external load (HOBOTECH, second-hand)
findings.value: about 85 W (vs 52 W for EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Specs, Testing, and Verdict – EcoFlow blog
findings.note: This is HOBOTECH's measurement as reported by EcoFlow, a competitor, on a page dated 2026-10-21. I did not open HOBOTECH's original. Treat it as the high end of a 58–85 W range.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC on
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra vs BLUETTI Elite 300 – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The review: 'the Elite 300 only consumed around 15 watts per hour while idling'. 15 W × 72 h = 1.08 kWh. The same page measured a full solar recharge of about 2.5 h in ideal sun. Our current page says 'about 19 W measured', which conflicts with this figure; check it.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy; UPS switchover
findings.value: 2.67 kWh out vs 3.49 kWh in (about 76% round trip); 8 ms switchover (8.25 ms on return)
findings.note: Kill-A-Watt readings, 0–100% charge and full discharge. Article dated 2026-08-27. The 76% is my arithmetic (2.67 ÷ 3.49). Freezer math: 2,670 Wh ÷ (15 W idle + 25 W freezer at 0.6 kWh/day) ≈ 67 h ≈ 2.8 days.

findings.label: Idle draw, AC on; efficiency
findings.value: about 22 W (idle-only runtime about 5.7 days); about 82% efficiency
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra vs BLUETTI Elite 300 – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The review: 'ran closer to 22 watts per hour'. Measured full solar recharge about 4 h in ideal sun. 22 W × 72 h = 1.58 kWh.

findings.label: Measured efficiency at near-maximum load; AC charge time
findings.value: about 89% at 3,650 W for 60 min; AC 0–100% in about 2 h 54 min (rated 2 h 20 min)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 review – The Solar Lab
findings.note: No idle figure, solar wattage or switchover time was measured. A 5,100 W surge held for nearly a minute. Page shows no date or author.
